title: fix(types): refuse a named view's stray kanban.groupBy at the object-view read door (objectui#10321)
body:
Fixes #10321
Clause-②: yes

Step 2 of 2 (step 1 was PR #10364). This adds the door: a named view on an `object-view` document that authors a stray `kanban.groupBy`, in either nesting, is now refused by name at the read door. The message is the one string the `list-view` route already gives. The texts that said the refusal "covers BOTH routes" now say what is true.

Ruling: objectui#8365 ruling B (「8365 同意」). It refuses a stored view's `kanban.groupBy` 「at the read door of the view, visible to the author of the view」, and this repo's mirror stops being more permissive than the spec. A named view's `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy` is a stored view authoring the same key, so it gets the same refusal.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/types`, `zod/objectql.zod.ts`**
  - New `checkNamedViewKanbanStrayGroupBy` on `ObjectViewSchema`, a sibling of `checkNamedViewCalendarAliases` on the same door (`.check(checkNamedViewCalendarAliases, checkNamedViewKanbanStrayGroupBy)`).
  - It reports `custom` at `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy` and at `listViews.KEY.options.kanban.groupBy`, and its message is read off `KanbanStrayGroupByRefusal.description`, so there is no second sentence.
  - Both checks walk `listViews` through one shared helper, `namedViewKindBlocks`. The calendar check's behaviour is unchanged (same nestings, order, keys and message), and so is the scope its docblock states.
  - `listViews` stays unmirrored: nothing enters `.shape`, `columns` is not required, and neither an undeclared sibling nor the legacy bag is refused.
  - The arm's "WHERE THIS ARM IS INSTALLED" docblock now lists both routes.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-view`, `ObjectView.tsx`**: `generateViewSchema`'s kanban-branch comment said the `KanbanConfig` refusal 「covers BOTH routes」. It now names where each route's door lives. Only a comment changed; the `renderListView` block is untouched (objectui#7924 holds a line there).
- **Pins**: new `packages/types/src/__tests__/named-view-kanban-stray-group-by-10321.test.ts`.
  - REFUSED arms, both nestings: `code` and `path`, a message EQUAL to the `list-view` route's, and one issue per written key. A multi-view arm checks that the issue lands on the right view key.
  - Controls: a dark control, two scope controls (an undeclared `swimlaneField` is kept; no `columns` required and the legacy bag accepted), and a sibling control (the calendar check still fires).
- **Test prose kept true**: the 9242 and 8355 plugin-view pins' docblocks, and one scope-control title ("nothing else about a named view is judged" became "nothing beyond the named alias refusals is judged").
- **Changesets**: new `.changeset/10321-named-view-kanban-groupby-refused.md` (`@object-ui/types: minor`, breaking semantics stated). Pending `8365-…` and `9242-…` changed in their bodies only; front matter is byte-identical (`cmp` exit 0 against `bff63cc12` for both).

## Premise, measured (zone 2)

All probes ran through `safeValidateSchema` on source, via tsx from the repo root. The spec probes used the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0.

- **D1** at base `bff63cc12` (before):
  - `object-view` `listViews.v1.kanban.groupBy` ⇒ ACCEPTED, key kept.
  - `listViews.v1.options.kanban.groupBy` ⇒ ACCEPTED, key kept.
  - Calendar lit controls ⇒ REFUSED `custom@listViews.v1.calendar.dateField` and `custom@listViews.v1.options.calendar.dateField`.
  - `list-view` controls ⇒ REFUSED `invalid_type@kanban.groupBy` and `custom@options.kanban.groupBy`.

  After (head): both named-view nestings ⇒ REFUSED `custom@listViews.v1.kanban.groupBy` and `custom@listViews.v1.options.kanban.groupBy`, with the same lead sentence. The dark control (`groupByField` only) and the undeclared-sibling control (`swimlaneField`) stay ACCEPTED, and the calendar and `list-view` readings are unchanged.
- **D2** holds: the `list-view` arm is `aliasKeyRefusal('groupBy', 'groupByField', 'this kanban configuration', …)` = `KanbanStrayGroupByRefusal`, plus the `ListViewSchema.options` check reading its `.description`. The new check reads the same `.description`.
- **D3**: the comment is rewritten as above.
- **D4** holds, with parity on both routes:
  - `ViewSchema` `listViews.v1.kanban` `{groupByField, columns, groupBy}` ⇒ REFUSED `unrecognized_keys@listViews.v1.kanban[groupBy]`, and the dark control `{groupByField, columns}` ⇒ ACCEPTED.
  - `ListViewSchema` `kanban` `{groupByField, columns, groupBy}` ⇒ REFUSED `unrecognized_keys@kanban[groupBy]`, and its dark control ⇒ ACCEPTED.
  - The spec refuses `options` wholesale on both routes (`listViews.v1.options` and `list-view` `options`, including an empty `{}` control). So refusing `options.kanban.groupBy` on a named view is no stricter than the spec, the same as on the `list-view` route.
  - Upstream answers `groupBy` as a plain unrecognized key. The "Did you mean `groupBy` → `groupByField`?" sentence is this repo's, which is what the ruling asked for.

## One deviation from the suggested route (zone 3), and why

The suggestion was to extend the existing calendar door with more arms. My first commit did exactly that (one function over a table of arms), and its ablation was sound. `check-changeset-claims` then led me to two PENDING changesets that describe that function by its scope, and both publish verbatim at the next release (#5400 is open):

- `8355-retire-calendar-date-aliases.md`: "It judges exactly the two spellings this entry retires, at the two nestings the producer merges".
- `9653-kanban-stray-groupby-refusal-text.md`: the docblock "now says … that the check judges the two calendar spellings only".

Folding kanban into that function would make both false at release, and neither file is in this claim's surface. A sibling check on the same `ObjectViewSchema` door keeps both literally true with no edit to either. It is still one door and still not a mirror, and the two checks share one walker.

## Pending-changeset sentences, before → after

`8365-stray-kanban-groupby-refused.md` (item 2's last sentence):
- before: "A named view's `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy` on an `object-view` document still validates green, in either nesting."
- after: "A named view's `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy` on an `object-view` document is not reached by this arm; objectui#10321 gives that route its own door, which refuses the key in either nesting with the same message."

`9242-stray-kanban-groupby-lane-second-route.md`:
1. before: "The reach of the contract half was measured rather than assumed, and on this route it does not narrow the affected population: the contract half landed with PR objectui#9236 and covers the **`list-view`** route only — … A named view's `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy`, the route this change repairs, gets no validating door from the contract half today: `safeValidateSchema` accepts it in either nesting and keeps the key. `tsc` refuses … on either. What this change repairs is therefore a pure **behaviour** gap, on any document that reaches this branch carrying the key, whether or not it passed through a validator."
   after: "The reach of the contract half was measured rather than assumed. PR objectui#9236 landed it on the **`list-view`** route — … A named view's `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy`, the route this change repairs, is not reached by that arm; it gets its own door separately (objectui#10321), which refuses the key in either nesting with the same message. `tsc` refuses … on either. A door reaches neither a document already in storage nor one that never passes through a validator, so what this change repairs is a pure **behaviour** gap, on any document that reaches this branch carrying the key."
2. before: "- **What an author can author today is unchanged** — this change touches no schema: a `list-view` document carrying the key is still refused, and a named view carrying it still validates green. On that route it is this branch, which now drops the key, that keeps the lane canonical."
   after: "- **What an author can author is unchanged by this change** — it touches no schema: a `list-view` document carrying the key is refused, and a named view carrying it is refused by the door objectui#10321 adds separately. For a document that carries the key anyway, it is this branch, which now drops the key, that keeps the lane canonical."
3. before: "Untouched, deliberately: the contract half (which covers the `list-view` route only), …"
   after: "Untouched, deliberately: the contract half (both routes' doors live in `@object-ui/types`), …"

## Verification, all at head `3291f15`

Every heavy command ran through `os-verify-lock.sh`, and each exit code was captured redirect-first.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/types/ packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.strayGroupByLane-9242.test.tsx packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.calendarAliasRefused-8355.test.tsx`: `Test Files 250 passed (250)`, `Tests 5372 passed (5372)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The 248 types test files include the new one, plus the 2 plugin-view pins.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new test file.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-view type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0.
  - The first attempt answered `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/components'`. That was a missing prerequisite in a fresh worktree, not a red gate.
  - It passed after `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/plugin-view^..." --concurrency=2`: `Tasks: 15 successful, 15 total`.
- ESLint, narrowed to the 5 changed TS/TSX files (`eslint --format json`): 5 files, 0 errors, 71 warnings, all pre-existing (the one in `objectql.zod.ts` is the explicit `any` in the `list-view` options check's record cast, present at base).
  - The narrowing is a measurement, not a skip: `eslint.config.js` sets no `projectService` / `parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and no untouched file's verdict can move.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.
- Gates, each exit 0:
  - `check-changeset-presence`: "5 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".
  - `check-changeset-claims`: "Every package declared across those 3 body(ies) is either not negated…". It is report-only; the 26 pending changesets naming touched files were read, see Acceptance notes.
  - `check-changeset-overwrite`: report-only. 8365 and 9242 declare the same packages and levels at base and now (case 2, a deliberate prose correction).
  - `check-pending-changeset-literals`, and `pnpm changeset:check` ("No changeset declares a `major` bump.").
  - `check-control-bytes` ("OK (scanned 8989 tracked text file(s)…)") and `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` ("VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)").
  - `check-installed-spec-pin-claims` (OK), `check-type-check-coverage`, `check-test-path-roots`, `pnpm check:spec-symbols` and `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources`.
  - `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all 8 paths: "NOT GOVERNED".

### Reverse verification (ablation, one-off, not kept as a test)

Run from a committed head through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which requires the anchor to hit and proves the restore. The subject is imported by relative path from source, so no `dist/` is in the resolution path.

- **Final structure, at `3291f15`**: `.check(checkNamedViewCalendarAliases, checkNamedViewKanbanStrayGroupBy);` → `.check(checkNamedViewCalendarAliases);`.
  - Proof it landed: anchor 1 → 0, blob `24dccfbaf111` → `da13eb853972`.
  - Predicted direction: REFUSED arms red, controls green. Observed: `named-view-kanban-stray-group-by-10321.test.ts (7 tests | 3 failed)`, and the 3 are exactly the REFUSED arms. The dark, scope and sibling controls stayed green, and the 8355 and 8365 files were fully green (`Tests 3 failed | 29 passed (32)`).
  - Restore: blob == HEAD `24dccfbaf111`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Superseded structure, at `dbe03f0`** (the table-driven version): deleting the kanban row gave the same direction, `3 failed | 27 passed (30)`, and the restore was proven the same way.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-view/` (the full package): `Test Files 51 passed (51)`, `Tests 485 passed (485)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

NOT MEASURED: CI (not awaited; the PM owns convergence).

## Overlap to know about

- **objectui#7928, ruled A today** (`pm:queue`, no PR yet): it flips `ObjectViewSchema.listViews` to a by-reference mirror of the spec's strict `ObjectListViewSchema`.
  - After that lands, `listViews.KEY.kanban.groupBy` also draws the spec's plain `unrecognized_keys`, which does not point at `groupByField`. This check still adds the ruled sentence, so it stays useful.
  - Its legacy-nesting half (`options.kanban`) becomes redundant with the wholesale `options` refusal, exactly like the calendar check's `options.calendar` half. That ruling already plans to invert the #8355 legacy-nesting pins, and the kanban scope-control arm that accepts a legacy bag without the stray key will need the same inversion.
  - Ordinary concurrency: whichever lands second merges `main`.
- **objectui#7924** edits `ObjectView.tsx`'s `renderListView` composition, a different region from the kanban-branch comment touched here.

## Acceptance notes

- **The shared message's explanatory tail is `list-view`-centric.** It says the key "reached `ListView`'s kanban branch" and "That branch now drops the key".
  - On the named-view route that is true when a host supplies `renderListView` (the node goes through `ListView`), and incomplete for `generateViewSchema`, which also drops the key (objectui#9242).
  - Kept verbatim on purpose: the dispatch asked for ONE string with no second sentence, and the pending `9653-…` changeset describes that tail as it stands.
  - Carrier: none (承接者:无).
- **Stale door list in unpublished test prose, not touched (outside this surface).** Two test headers still name the old door list that step 1 corrected in the 8365 changeset:
  - `ListView.strayGroupByRefused-8365.test.tsx` (plugin-list) says `safeValidateSchema` is "the same entry point the CLI's `os check` / `os validate` and the VS Code extension run".
  - `calendar-date-alias-refusal-8355.test.ts` (types) says "`os check` / `os validate` / the save gate all run `safeValidateSchema`".
  - Carrier: none (承接者:无).
- **The changeset-claims read.**
  - 26 pending changesets name `objectql.zod.ts` or `ObjectView.tsx`. The only ones that speak to the named-view door or the kanban refusal's reach are 8355, 9653, 8365 and 9242.
  - 8365 and 9242 are edited above. 8355 and 9653 stay true because of the sibling design. `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md` ("`listViews` stays unmirrored") stays true.
- **No doc edit.** No README or guide teaches a named view's `kanban` block, and the refusal message carries its own remedy.
